# Angular Service Standards

**Load at**: Module 7 (Service Implementation)
**Applies to**: All Angular services generated by the `angular-ui` agent

---

## 1. Service Structure

### Injectable Decorator
```typescript
// Root-provided (default for most services)
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })

// Component-provided (when service state should be per-component-instance)
@Injectable() // + added to component's providers array

// Module-provided (NgModule apps only)
@Injectable({ providedIn: SomeModule })
```

Default to `providedIn: 'root'` unless the user's architecture requires scoped services.

### Class Structure (in order)
```typescript
@Injectable({ providedIn: 'root' })
export class [FeatureName]Service {

  // 1. Injected dependencies (private readonly)
  private readonly http = inject(HttpClient);

  // 2. Private state (BehaviorSubjects or signals)
  private readonly _data = new BehaviorSubject<[Type] | null>(null);

  // 3. Public observables (exposed from private subjects)
  readonly data$ = this._data.asObservable();

  // 4. Private constants (URLs, keys)
  private readonly baseUrl = `${environment.apiBaseUrl}/[endpoint]`;

  // 5. Public methods
  getAll(): Observable<...> { ... }
  getById(id: string): Observable<...> { ... }
  create(payload: ...): Observable<...> { ... }
  update(id: string, payload: ...): Observable<...> { ... }
  delete(id: string): Observable<...> { ... }

  // 6. Private helpers
  private handleError(error: HttpErrorResponse): Observable<never> { ... }
}
```

---

## 2. Observable Patterns

### Preferred: return Observables
```typescript
// ✅ Return Observable — consumer controls subscription
getUsers(): Observable<User[]> {
  return this.http.get<User[]>(this.baseUrl);
}
```

### Never: subscribe inside service (except for fire-and-forget side effects)
```typescript
// ❌ Wrong — service subscribes, loses error propagation
getUsers(): void {
  this.http.get<User[]>(this.baseUrl).subscribe(users => {
    this._users.next(users);
  });
}
```

### RxJS operator chain pattern
```typescript
return this.http.post<Response>(this.baseUrl, payload).pipe(
  tap(response => this._cache.next(response)),   // side effect
  catchError(this.handleError.bind(this)),        // error transform
  finalize(() => this._isLoading.next(false))     // always runs
);
```

---

## 3. State Management in Services

### RxJS approach (recommended for most cases)
```typescript
private readonly _items = new BehaviorSubject<Item[]>([]);
private readonly _isLoading = new BehaviorSubject<boolean>(false);
private readonly _error = new BehaviorSubject<string | null>(null);

readonly items$ = this._items.asObservable();
readonly isLoading$ = this._isLoading.asObservable();
readonly error$ = this._error.asObservable();
```

### Signals approach (Angular 21+, confirmed in Module 0)
```typescript
private readonly _items = signal<Item[]>([]);
private readonly _isLoading = signal(false);

readonly items = this._items.asReadonly();
readonly isLoading = this._isLoading.asReadonly();
```

### Cache pattern (avoid redundant API calls)
```typescript
private cachedItems: Item[] | null = null;

getItems(): Observable<Item[]> {
  if (this.cachedItems) {
    return of(this.cachedItems);
  }
  return this.http.get<Item[]>(this.baseUrl).pipe(
    tap(items => { this.cachedItems = items; })
  );
}

clearCache(): void {
  this.cachedItems = null;
}
```

---

## 4. Error Handling

Standard error handler (copy to every service):
```typescript
private handleError(error: HttpErrorResponse): Observable<never> {
  let message: string;

  if (error.status === 0) {
    message = 'Network error — please check your connection.';
  } else {
    // Use API error message if available, otherwise generic by status
    message = error.error?.message
      ?? error.error?.error
      ?? `Error ${error.status}: ${error.statusText}`;
  }

  this._error.next(message);
  return throwError(() => new Error(message));
}
```

---

## 5. TypeScript Standards

- NEVER use `any` for HTTP response types — define interfaces
- Use generic HttpClient methods: `this.http.get<ResponseType>(url)`
- Use `Partial<T>` for update payloads (not all fields required)
- Use `Pick<T, 'field1' | 'field2'>` for projection types

---

## 6. Environment Config

```typescript
// ✅ Correct — use environment config
private readonly baseUrl = `${environment.apiBaseUrl}/users`;

// ❌ Wrong — never hardcode in service
private readonly baseUrl = 'https://api.example.com/users';
```

For hackathons without environment files yet:
```typescript
// TODO: move to environment.ts before production
const API_BASE = 'http://localhost:3000';
private readonly baseUrl = `${API_BASE}/users`;
```

---

## 7. What NOT to Do

- Do NOT use `Promise` — use `Observable` (Angular HTTP is Observable-based)
- Do NOT use `subscribe()` inside a service method (return Observables instead)
- Do NOT ignore errors — always use `catchError`
- Do NOT forget `finalize` when managing loading state
- Do NOT store sensitive data (tokens, passwords) in service state
- Do NOT make services stateful when they can be stateless
